# Superhuman Email Browsing UX Specification

Desktop reference specification, excluding AI and calendar functionality.

**Status:** Evidence-backed specification with explicitly proposed interaction details. This is not a verified behavioral clone.

## Scope and interpretation

The target is the Superhuman desktop email experience shown in the supplied screenshot, cross-checked against the installed macOS application, version `1041.0.45`. The deliverable describes the experience of navigating, finding, opening, reading, and triaging existing email, rather than composing or sending it.

- **Included:** Inbox splits, conversation lists, focus and selection, conversation reading, contact context, search, folder and label browsing, native tabs and accounts, attachment viewing, manual triage, manual email reminders, and recovery.
- **Excluded:** All AI functionality, automatic classification logic, automatic summaries, generated replies, agent integrations, calendar views, availability, scheduling, meeting RSVP experiences, and event creation.
- **Boundary:** Reply, Reply All, Forward, and Compose may remain exit points from browsing. Their editor behavior, sending, templates, and signatures are not specified.
- **Manual reminders:** Included as an email snooze/triage mechanism, not as calendar functionality. Automatic reminders are excluded.
- **Existing badges:** Existing labels may be rendered as metadata. Reproducing the AI mechanism that generated an existing label is out of scope.
- **Platform:** Desktop/macOS first. Mobile gestures and responsive mobile layouts are not part of this specification.

### Evidence labels

Each requirement distinguishes recovered information from completion choices.

| Label | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `V` | Visual observation from the supplied screenshot; establishes appearance, not interaction |
| `B` | Binary-based / source-assisted observation from shipped Electron resources; static, not executed |
| `D` | Documentation-based behavior from the cited material |
| `P` | Proposed implementation contract where direct target behavior is not established |
| `U` | Unresolved fidelity question requiring a live target observation |

`D` is not equivalent to testing version 1041.0.45. Public documentation may describe a different renderer release or account capability.

### Investigation boundary

The installed Electron ASAR was inspected with the skill-pinned `rea-agents@6.5.0` runtime. Its selected source includes the native shell and production origin configuration, not a recovered authenticated mail renderer. Native tab and history code supplies limited shell evidence.

An authenticated live browsing session was not available: Comet displayed Superhuman's “Get Started Now” screen, and no Superhuman/Electron listening endpoint was found by a bounded local check. The application was not restarted, its debugging configuration was not changed, and no credentials, cookies, mail caches, or account databases were extracted.

The supplied screenshot is the only observed authenticated screen. No mail was opened, sent, archived, relabeled, or deleted during the investigation.

## Product model

The central interaction model is a sequence of actionable conversations, organized into focused inbox views, with fast transitions into individual messages. Split Inboxes are not storage folders: they represent email requiring attention, whereas folders organize stored email. (`D`; [Default Split Inbox](https://help.superhuman.com/hc/en-us/articles/46005619081101-Default-Split-Inbox))

The three distinctions below are essential to a faithful implementation:

- **Focused versus selected:** One conversation is the current keyboard target; a separate collection can be selected for bulk actions. Superhuman documents `X`, range-extension keys, and modifier-click selection. (`D`; [Multiselect](https://new.superhuman.com/multiselect-29111))
- **Conversation versus message:** Conversation navigation uses `J`/`K`, while message navigation within a conversation uses `N`/`P`; individual messages can be expanded. (`D`; [Shortcut reference](https://nickgray.net/superhuman/), [Attachments](https://help.superhuman.com/hc/en-us/articles/46005568142989-Attachments))
- **Contact pane versus message preview:** The screenshot's right pane contains sender information, not the email body. Documentation confirms that selecting an inbox conversation shows contact context in that sidebar. (`V`, `D`; [Contact Pane](https://help.superhuman.com/hc/en-us/articles/46005778939789-Contact-Pane))

### Conceptual navigation hierarchy

This is a UX model, not a recovered internal schema.

```text
Native window
  Native tab
    Active email account
      Browsing context
        Inbox split | Folder | Label | Search results
          Focused conversation
          Bulk-selected conversation IDs
          Open conversation
            Focused message
            Expanded message IDs
            Active contact
            Attachment preview
```

Account identity, list context, and message identity must remain separate. A conversation can appear in more than one split when configured to also appear in Important or Other. (`D`; [Default Split Inbox](https://help.superhuman.com/hc/en-us/articles/46005619081101-Default-Split-Inbox))

## Information architecture and layout

### Reference screen anatomy

The original image is 1028 × 1290 pixels. The geometry below uses image coordinates, not CSS pixels; device scale, capture scaling, and native window padding are unknown. All measurements are approximate. (`V`)

| Region | Reference-image geometry | Visual contract |
|---|---|---|
| Native tab/title strip | Top approximately 41 px | Thin, low-contrast strip showing view, count, and account |
| Application rail | Left approximately 40 px | Narrow persistent icon column, separated from the main surface |
| Main browsing surface | Approximately x=40–756 | Wide list area with its own top navigation |
| Contact/context pane | Approximately x=758–1027, about 270 px | Darker full-height side surface, separated by a thin vertical divider |
| Split navigation | Approximately y=76–90 | Inline split names with counts and an emphasized active split |
| First conversation | Approximately y=119–155 | Compact single-line row with focus treatment |
| Conversation rhythm | Approximately 36 px | Dense scanning rhythm; no card stack or large avatars |
| Date grouping | Between the third and fourth displayed conversations | Muted group caption with extra vertical separation |

The screenshot shows six rows in the active split, with considerable empty space below rather than stretched rows. It also shows a hamburger/menu control before the split names, compact compose/search controls after them, and utility controls at the bottom of the contact pane. (`V`)

### Main list composition

The visible column sequence is sender, optional label badges, subject, snippet, and trailing date/actions. The focused row uses a soft gray full-row background and a narrow lavender bar on the left; sender names are more visually prominent than preview text. (`V`)

```text
| focus | sender     | labels | subject      | preview text... | date/actions |
```

- **Sender column:** Fixed or constrained width; long names truncate without shifting the other rows. The screenshot contains truncated sender names. (`V`)
- **Label column:** Compact colored chips before the subject; no interpretation of the label text is required. (`V`)
- **Subject/snippet:** Occupy a single horizontal line in this reference; the preview has lower contrast and truncates at available width. (`V`)
- **Trailing area:** Unfocused rows display dates; the focused row displays several compact action icons instead. The icon identities and whether focus or pointer hover causes the replacement are not verified. (`V`, `U`)
- **Group headers:** Render chronological captions such as “Earlier this month” without turning them into selectable conversations. Exact bucket boundaries and timezone rules remain unknown. (`V`, `U`)

### Visual tokens

These are reconstruction starting values sampled from the JPEG, not recovered design-system tokens. Sampling and compression can alter apparent colors. (`V`)

| Token | Approximate reference |
|---|---|
| Main surface | `#292826` |
| Contact surface | `#1F1E1C` |
| Focus-row fill | Approximately `#474644` |
| Focus accent | Approximately `#BBA5ED` |
| Dividers | Low-contrast warm gray; about one image pixel |
| Typography | Compact sans-serif; exact family, CSS size, and weight unresolved |
| Corner treatment | Slight row rounding; avoid large rounded cards |
| Text hierarchy | Primary off-white; secondary warm gray; labels supply localized color |

Do not infer that all bold rows are unread. The screenshot does not establish the mapping between read state and text weight. (`U`)

### Reconstruction layout policy

The following fills gaps rather than asserting target behavior:

- **List mode:** Keep the rail, main list, and contact pane visible on a sufficiently wide desktop viewport. (`P`)
- **Reading mode:** Replace the main list region with the conversation reader while retaining a clear back path and contact context. Do not invent a permanent side-by-side email preview based on the screenshot. The exact target reader geometry remains unverified. (`P`, `U`)
- **Narrow desktop:** Allow subject/snippet width to contract first. Below a chosen breakpoint, collapse contact context into an explicitly opened panel rather than crushing the list; this breakpoint is a product choice, not a recovered value. (`P`)
- **Calendar removal:** Omit the screenshot's calendar rail item, calendar split, and calendar utilities from this bounded implementation. Preserve email navigation without leaving dead controls. (`P`)
- **AI removal:** Omit AI destinations, summary space, generated suggestions, and AI commands entirely. Do not reserve empty layout slots for them. (`P`)

## Inbox splits and folder navigation

### Split tabs

Split names appear across the top of the inbox; the active split is emphasized. The screenshot's active “Other” view displays a count of six. (`V`)

Split badges represent total conversations, not unread conversations. Counts disappear at zero and above 999, rather than displaying zero or an arbitrarily invented “999+” badge. (`D`; [Default Split Inbox](https://help.superhuman.com/hc/en-us/articles/46005619081101-Default-Split-Inbox))

- **Change split:** `Tab` moves to the next split and `Shift+Tab` to the previous split. Pointer selection is an implementation contract consistent with the visible tabs; wraparound behavior is unresolved. (`D`, `P`, `U`; [Default Split Inbox](https://help.superhuman.com/hc/en-us/articles/46005619081101-Default-Split-Inbox))
- **Empty split visibility:** Optional splits can hide when empty; Inbox, Important, and Other cannot use this setting. A hidden split remains accessible through “go to [split name].” (`D`; [Default Split Inbox](https://help.superhuman.com/hc/en-us/articles/46005619081101-Default-Split-Inbox))
- **Overlapping membership:** A split can also show its conversations in Important/Other, depending on configuration. Do not force every split into a mutually exclusive folder model. (`D`; [Default Split Inbox](https://help.superhuman.com/hc/en-us/articles/46005619081101-Default-Split-Inbox))
- **Disable split:** Conversations return to the appropriate Inbox/Important/Other views. Removing a view is not deleting its email. (`D`; [Default Split Inbox](https://help.superhuman.com/hc/en-us/articles/46005619081101-Default-Split-Inbox))

Configuration screens themselves are secondary to browsing. If included, support naming and rule-based custom definitions, ordering, hiding when empty, and enabling/disabling; exclude Auto Label configuration. Custom definitions can use structured criteria, but direct body-keyword definitions are not supported by the documented workflow. (`D`; [Custom Split Inbox](https://help.superhuman.com/hc/en-us/articles/46005636204941-Custom-Split-Inbox))

### Folder and label navigator

From the inbox, the left arrow reveals folders/labels, and the command palette supports “go to [folder]” or “go to [label].” (`D`; [Folders](https://help.superhuman.com/hc/en-us/articles/46005732666253-Folders), [Labels](https://help.superhuman.com/hc/en-us/articles/46005736546061-Labels))

- **Destinations:** Support Inbox, Starred, Sent, Drafts as a browsing destination only, Done, Reminders, Spam, Trash, All Mail, provider folders/labels, and Muted where supported. These destination names are documented, but their exact visual order is not recovered. (`D`, `U`; [Mac shortcut sheet](https://download.superhuman.com/Superhuman%20Keyboard%20Shortcuts.pdf))
- **Large folder collections:** Current label documentation describes nine folders followed by “Show more.” Treat this as current documentation, not a confirmed property of the installed renderer. (`D`; [Labels](https://help.superhuman.com/hc/en-us/articles/46005736546061-Labels))
- **Return contract:** Opening a destination replaces the main list context, updates its title, and clears cross-context bulk selection. Save the old context for Back. (`P`)
- **Empty destination:** Show a context-specific empty message; do not show an inbox-zero celebration for a failed search or an empty Spam folder. (`P`)

### Native tabs and accounts

Native tabs are independent browsing workspaces, not a unified inbox. Official documentation explicitly describes using one tab per account as a workaround for the absence of a unified inbox. (`D`; [Unified Inbox Workaround](https://help.superhuman.com/hc/en-us/articles/46005722297229-Unified-Inbox-Workaround))

The shipped shell statically contains tab switching with focus transfer and Back behavior that avoids handling the command when an editable element is focused. It also configures `https://mail.superhuman.com` as its production application origin. These are shell observations, not proof of mail-renderer behavior. (`B`)

- **Tab commands:** New tab is `Cmd+T`; next/previous tabs are `Cmd+Shift+]` / `Cmd+Shift+[`; numeric switching uses `Cmd+1`, `Cmd+2`, and so on. (`D`; [Unified Inbox Workaround](https://help.superhuman.com/hc/en-us/articles/46005722297229-Unified-Inbox-Workaround))
- **Tab title:** View/split name, count, and account appear in the native tab title; user-defined tab renaming is not documented as supported. (`V`, `D`; [Unified Inbox Workaround](https://help.superhuman.com/hc/en-us/articles/46005722297229-Unified-Inbox-Workaround))
- **Account switch:** Provide “Switch Account(s)” through the palette. Do not silently search all accounts or merge their conversation IDs. (`D`, `P`; [Unified Inbox Workaround](https://help.superhuman.com/hc/en-us/articles/46005722297229-Unified-Inbox-Workaround))

## List focus, opening, and selection

### State distinctions

A minimal implementation needs `focusedThreadId`, `selectedThreadIds`, `openThreadId`, `activeMessageId`, and `expandedMessageIds`. These are proposed model names, not extracted application identifiers. (`P`)

| State | Meaning | Rendering and action target |
|---|---|---|
| No focus | List has no active conversation | No stale contact or destructive action target |
| Focused conversation | Current keyboard target | Highlighted row; contact pane represents that conversation |
| Hovered conversation | Pointer target only | Optional action affordances; do not imply bulk selection |
| Bulk selection | Explicitly selected set | Selection markers and count; bulk actions target the set |
| Open conversation | Reader is active | Message-level navigation becomes available |

The screenshot establishes one visibly focused row. It does not establish whether hovering transfers keyboard focus, whether a first click focuses or opens, or whether opening automatically marks the thread read. (`V`, `U`)

### Proposed pointer and focus contracts

These contracts make an implementation deterministic until live fidelity tests can replace them:

- **Row click:** Open the conversation; keyboard focus alone remains available without opening it. (`P`)
- **Pointer hover:** Reveal row controls without changing the bulk-selected set or read state. (`P`)
- **Inline action click:** Act on that row and stop propagation so the reader does not open accidentally. (`P`)
- **Keyboard movement:** `J`/`K` move the conversation focus; scroll just enough to keep the focused row visible. Do not wrap at list boundaries by default. (`D` for the keys, `P` for scrolling/boundaries; [Shortcut reference](https://nickgray.net/superhuman/))
- **Open/return:** `Enter` opens the focused conversation; Back restores the exact context, focused ID, and approximate scroll position rather than resetting to the first row. (`D` for Enter, `P` for restoration; [Shortcut reference](https://nickgray.net/superhuman/))
- **Unread handling:** Focus and hover do not change read state. For an implementation, opening a loaded conversation may mark it read once; exact target timing, delay, and partial-thread rules remain unresolved. (`P`, `U`)
- **Conversation removed:** Prefer the next surviving row, then the previous row, then an empty state. Do not retain an invisible destructive-action target. (`P`)

### Bulk selection

Superhuman documents `X` to select a conversation, `Shift+J`/`Shift+K` to extend selection, and Cmd/Shift-click to select multiple conversations. (`D`; [Multiselect](https://new.superhuman.com/multiselect-29111))

For reconstruction, selection should use stable IDs rather than row positions; plain navigation should not silently select additional items. Escape should clear the selected set before leaving the list, and the UI should display how many conversations a bulk operation will affect. These exact restoration, anchor, and Escape rules are proposed. (`P`)

“Select all,” “select all from here,” and cross-page selection must not be conflated. The official shortcut sheet names both selection actions, but their precise unloaded-results semantics were not tested; do not claim a loaded-page selection covers every matching email. (`D`, `U`; [Mac shortcut sheet](https://download.superhuman.com/Superhuman%20Keyboard%20Shortcuts.pdf))

## Conversation reading

### Reader content and hierarchy

The reader must distinguish conversation-level metadata from message-level metadata. The presence of message selection, expansion, attachment selection, and per-message read-status surfaces is documented, but the full reader layout is not visible in the supplied screenshot. (`D`, `U`; [Attachments](https://help.superhuman.com/hc/en-us/articles/46005568142989-Attachments), [Read Statuses](https://help.superhuman.com/hc/en-us/articles/46005603745293-Read-Statuses-and-Recent-Opens-Feed))

Use the following hierarchy as a proposed implementation:

```text
Conversation header
  Back / current browsing context
  Subject and labels
  Conversation-level triage actions
Message stack
  Collapsed message header
  Expanded message
    Sender / recipients / timestamp / details affordance
    Original email body
    Attachment chips
    Optional read-status indicator
Browsing exit points
  Reply / Reply All / Forward
Contact/context pane
```

- **Message focus:** `N`/`P` move between messages. The focused message can use a purple left bar, as described in attachment documentation. (`D`; [Attachments](https://help.superhuman.com/hc/en-us/articles/46005568142989-Attachments))
- **Expansion:** `O` expands a message and `Shift+O` expands all messages according to the shortcut reference. Exact collapse toggling, initial expansion, and initial scroll position remain unverified. (`D`, `U`; [Shortcut reference](https://nickgray.net/superhuman/))
- **Default presentation:** For a reconstruction, expand the most recent relevant message and collapse older history, while preserving any expansion made by the user during that visit. This is a completion choice, not recovered behavior. (`P`)
- **Header details:** Provide a disclosure for full sender/recipient addresses and timestamps without requiring a new page. Exact field ordering and menu design remain unresolved. (`P`, `U`)
- **Long email:** Scroll the message body within the reading surface without moving the rail and losing the back affordance. Exact original scroll-container behavior is unverified. (`P`)
- **Message rendering:** Render original email content, not a generated summary. Quoted-history disclosure, remote images, sanitization policy, tracking protection defaults, and dark-mode transformations require separate validation. (`P`, `U`)
- **Next conversation:** `J`/`K` navigate conversations in the originating list, not messages within the current conversation. Preserve the search/filter/split that defined that list. (`D` for key meaning, `P` for origin preservation; [Shortcut reference](https://nickgray.net/superhuman/))

### Contact pane

The contact pane can show a name, avatar, email, location, bio, social/site links, and links to four recent emails. It appears for the selected inbox conversation and when hovering over a person's name/address in a header. (`D`; [Contact Pane](https://help.superhuman.com/hc/en-us/articles/46005778939789-Contact-Pane))

- **Sparse profile:** The screenshot shows only name, email, and a website. Missing enrichment should not produce placeholder prose or a broken profile layout. (`V`, `P`)
- **Search from contact:** Clicking the contact name searches for other email from that person. Clicking their email address starts a draft, which is an out-of-scope exit point here. (`D`; [Contact Pane](https://help.superhuman.com/hc/en-us/articles/46005778939789-Contact-Pane))
- **Copy affordances:** Hovering a name or email exposes a copy control. Keep copying distinct from navigation and drafting. (`D`; [Contact Pane](https://help.superhuman.com/hc/en-us/articles/46005778939789-Contact-Pane))
- **Contact switching:** For a reconstruction, hovering another participant temporarily changes contact context; leaving restores the active participant unless the user explicitly navigates. Exact pinning/restoration is unresolved. (`P`, `U`)
- **Visibility:** Documentation says the contact pane cannot currently be disabled. Any collapsible responsive variant in an implementation is a departure, not a recovered preference. (`D`, `P`; [Contact Pane](https://help.superhuman.com/hc/en-us/articles/46005778939789-Contact-Pane))

### Attachments and links

`Cmd+O` is the documented shortcut for opening links/attachments; PDF attachments can preview inside Superhuman. Other formats can open system/browser previews or download, with behavior varying by format, browser, and OS. (`D`; [Attachments](https://help.superhuman.com/hc/en-us/articles/46005568142989-Attachments))

- **PDF:** Support in-app preview rather than implying that every document type has the same reader. (`D`; [Attachments](https://help.superhuman.com/hc/en-us/articles/46005568142989-Attachments))
- **Unsupported preview:** Word, Excel, PowerPoint, HTML, and cloud links must not be advertised as supported in-app document viewers. Offer the documented external/download path. (`D`; [Attachments](https://help.superhuman.com/hc/en-us/articles/46005568142989-Attachments))
- **Attachment menu:** Right-clicking an attachment chip supports Copy Link/Open Link. The exact visual menu and keyboard chooser are not recovered. (`D`, `U`; [Attachments](https://help.superhuman.com/hc/en-us/articles/46005568142989-Attachments))
- **Return contract:** Dismissing a preview restores the same message, expansion state, and scroll position. Loading/error states must not make the underlying thread unreachable. (`P`)
- **External effects:** Opening a link, downloading a file, and opening an executable are separate actions. An attachment preview must never imply automatic execution. (`P`)

### Optional sent-mail context

Read statuses are a non-AI browsing feature. Documentation places detail popovers on the checkmarks at the right of an email header and under the last message, and describes a Recent Opens sidebar with links into conversations. (`D`; [Read Statuses](https://help.superhuman.com/hc/en-us/articles/46005603745293-Read-Statuses-and-Recent-Opens-Feed))

Treat these as optional and account/plan-dependent. A read receipt from a recipient is not the same state as whether the local user has read a conversation; a reconstruction must keep the two concepts separate. (`D` for capability conditions, `P` for state design; [Read Statuses](https://help.superhuman.com/hc/en-us/articles/46005603745293-Read-Statuses-and-Recent-Opens-Feed))

## Search and command discovery

### Command palette

`Cmd+K` opens Superhuman Command; actions display shortcuts on the right, and button-hover tooltips also teach shortcuts. Documentation says shortcuts are not currently customizable. (`D`; [Keyboard Shortcuts](https://help.superhuman.com/hc/en-us/articles/REDACTED))

For reconstruction, use a focused text input, a keyboard-navigable results list, a visibly active result, and contextual commands for the focused conversation or selected set. Enter executes the active command; Escape closes the palette and restores its origin focus. Ranking, fuzzy matching, initial suggested commands, and nested-menu behavior remain unverified. (`P`, `U`)

Remove AI and calendar commands from this bounded command catalog. This is intentional scope reduction, not a claim that those commands are absent in Superhuman. (`P`)

### Search flow

`/` starts search, and the documented flow accepts a query followed by Enter. Search covers the inbox and folders, with common operators shown in the right-hand sidebar. (`D`; [Search](https://help.superhuman.com/hc/en-us/articles/46005672652301-Search), [Keyboard Shortcuts](https://help.superhuman.com/hc/en-us/articles/REDACTED))

```text
Browsing context
  -> Search input + operator guidance
  -> Enter
  -> Results list
  -> Open conversation
  -> Back to the same results and query
  -> Back to previous browsing context
```

The transitions and preservation of result focus are proposed contracts. Autocomplete, live-result timing, result ranking, hit highlighting, and whether the list updates before Enter are unresolved. (`P`, `U`)

- **Query semantics:** Adjacent terms combine with AND; `OR` broadens the query; quoted phrases request exact matching; a leading hyphen excludes a term. (`D`; [Search](https://help.superhuman.com/hc/en-us/articles/46005672652301-Search))
- **Structured criteria:** Rule-based splits document `From:`, `To:`, `Subject:`, `Bcc:`, and `Cc:` criteria, while labels can be browsed/searched using `label:`. A complete search grammar is not recovered. (`D`, `U`; [Custom Split Inbox](https://help.superhuman.com/hc/en-us/articles/46005636204941-Custom-Split-Inbox), [Labels](https://help.superhuman.com/hc/en-us/articles/46005736546061-Labels))
- **Result treatment:** Reuse conversation rows and keyboard navigation rather than introducing a separate card system. Retain the query while opening and closing a result. (`P`)
- **No results:** Show the query, a clear no-match message, and an immediate way to edit or clear it. Do not conflate zero results with offline incompleteness. (`P`)
- **Offline search:** Recent cached email can be searched offline; this does not establish a complete local copy of the mailbox. (`D`; [Search](https://help.superhuman.com/hc/en-us/articles/46005672652301-Search))
- **Account scope:** Default reconstruction scope is the active account. Cross-account search was not established and should not be promised. (`P`, `U`)

## Triage while browsing

These operations are part of the browse-and-process loop, but were not executed on the user's mailbox. Documented effects are listed separately from the proposed immediate UI response.

| Action | Documented meaning | Proposed UI response |
|---|---|---|
| Mark Done | Archive, not delete; remove from inbox and retain searchability; a new reply brings the thread back. (`D`; [Mark Done](https://help.superhuman.com/hc/en-us/articles/47439134613773-Mark-Done)) | Remove from inbox-context lists, update affected split counts, move focus to a surviving neighbor, offer Undo. (`P`) |
| Mark Not Done | Supported conversation action in the shortcut reference. (`D`; [Shortcut reference](https://nickgray.net/superhuman/)) | Restore inbox membership and invalidate affected view counts; preserve independent star/label/read states. (`P`) |
| Star | Supported on a conversation and in bulk. (`D`; [Multiselect](https://new.superhuman.com/multiselect-29111)) | Toggle indicator without opening the reader; remove from Starred only when the view's membership changes. (`P`) |
| Read/unread | Supported conversation action. (`D`; [Shortcut reference](https://nickgray.net/superhuman/)) | Update read styling independently of focus and archive state; remove only from filters that no longer match. (`P`) |
| Label | Apply/remove a tag without removing the conversation from the inbox. (`D`; [Labels](https://help.superhuman.com/hc/en-us/articles/46005736546061-Labels)) | Update badges and relevant label views, preserving the current browsing position. (`P`) |
| Move | Gmail label destination applies a label plus Done; Outlook Move targets folders, not category labels. (`D`; [Labels](https://help.superhuman.com/hc/en-us/articles/46005736546061-Labels)) | Show provider-appropriate destinations; never conflate a tag with a folder. (`P`) |
| Remind Me | Remove from inbox into pending Reminders; return at the scheduled time under the chosen reply condition. (`D`; [Remind Me](https://help.superhuman.com/hc/en-us/articles/46005666142733-Remind-Me)) | Show manual time input and condition, then update membership and provide undo/recovery. (`P`) |
| Mute | Gmail conversations leave the inbox and can be unmuted; Outlook muting is not documented as supported. (`D`; [Muting Conversations](https://help.superhuman.com/hc/en-us/articles/46005597483661-Muting-Conversations)) | Only offer where supported; never show an action that silently fails for the provider. (`P`) |
| Trash | Move to Trash; the app does not offer emptying Trash directly. (`D`; [Unwanted Emails](https://help.superhuman.com/hc/en-us/articles/46005635358349-Dealing-with-Unwanted-Emails)) | Distinguish from Done and from permanent deletion. Preserve a recovery path. (`P`) |
| Important / Other | Can affect one conversation, all current/future mail from an address, or a domain where supported. (`D`; [Moving Conversations](https://help.superhuman.com/hc/en-us/articles/46005707869965-Moving-Conversations-Between-Important-and-Other)) | Require an explicit scope choice; never silently promote a one-thread action into a rule. (`P`) |
| Unsubscribe / Spam / Block | Distinct options, including sender/domain scope and optional bulk archive/trash; unsubscribe may invoke an external page or send a request. (`D`; [Unwanted Emails](https://help.superhuman.com/hc/en-us/articles/46005635358349-Dealing-with-Unwanted-Emails)) | Display the exact action and affected scope before committing the broader operation. (`P`) |

### Undo and optimistic updates

Desktop Undo uses `Z` within a documented 10-second window. Do not substitute the native text-editing `Cmd+Z` shortcut for this browsing action. (`D`; [Undo](https://help.superhuman.com/hc/en-us/articles/46005666743309-Undo))

For reconstruction, apply ordinary triage optimistically, retain a reversible action record, show a concise confirmation with Undo, and roll back on provider failure. Exact toast position, stacking, animation, multi-action history, and original failure UI were not recovered. (`P`, `U`)

### Manual reminder details

## State, consistency, and resilience

### Suggested state model

This model supports the specified UX without claiming a recovered implementation or backend API.

```typescript
type BrowseContext =
  | { kind: "split"; accountId: string; splitId: string }
  | { kind: "folder"; accountId: string; folderId: string }
  | { kind: "label"; accountId: string; labelId: string }
  | { kind: "search"; accountId: string; query: string };

type TabBrowseState = {
  context: BrowseContext;
  filter: null | "unread" | "starred" | "important" | "no-reply";
  orderedThreadIds: string[];
  focusedThreadId: string | null;
  selectedThreadIds: Set<string>;
  rangeAnchorThreadId: string | null;
  openThreadId: string | null;
  activeMessageId: string | null;
  expandedMessageIds: Set<string>;
  listScrollOffset: number;
  readerScrollOffset: number;
  overlay: null | "command" | "search-input" | "label" |
```

The four filter names are present in the official shortcut sheet; their exact combination rules and defaults are unresolved. For a bounded implementation, use one active filter at a time until live behavior establishes otherwise. (`D`, `P`, `U`; [Mac shortcut sheet](https://download.superhuman.com/Superhuman%20Keyboard%20Shortcuts.pdf))

### Required consistency invariants

All invariants here are proposed engineering contracts:

- **Stable identity:** Focus and selection attach to conversation IDs, not indexes; incoming rows cannot redirect an action to a different thread.
- **Account isolation:** Every action carries the active account identity; one account's thread IDs or selection never leak into another.
- **Independent dimensions:** Read, star, labels, inbox membership, reminder, and mute are separate state dimensions.
- **Derived views:** Update every visible view that shares a conversation, not just the list where an action started.
- **Preserved origin:** Back from a conversation restores split/folder/label/query/filter and the best surviving anchor.
- **Async safety:** Ignore stale search responses from older queries; a slow response cannot overwrite a newer results context.
- **Failure recovery:** Roll back failed optimistic changes, announce the failure, and preserve a retry path.
- **New mail stability:** Avoid shifting the focused item under the user during triage; the exact Superhuman arrival/banner policy is unknown.

### Non-happy-path states

| State | Proposed treatment |
|---|---|
| Initial loading | Preserve shell geometry and avoid displaying cached counters as confirmed fresh data |
| Empty split | Clear focus, selection, and contact context; show a split-specific completed state |
| No search matches | Keep query editable; distinguish no match from incomplete/offline results |
| Offline cached list | Allow reading cached content; make freshness/availability boundaries clear |
| Message not cached | Keep the conversation header/back path; show unavailable body with retry |
| Conversation removed elsewhere | Return to a valid list anchor; avoid a dead reader with active triage buttons |
| Mutation failure | Restore the affected state and report failure without losing navigation |
| Partial bulk failure | Distinguish succeeded and failed IDs; do not report the whole operation as successful |
| Empty contact profile | Render only known fields, with no invented enrichment |
| Attachment error | Dismiss/retry/open externally without losing the thread |
| Account authentication required | Keep local navigation state but stop claiming remote actions succeeded |

Offline recent-email search is documented; the rest of this table is a proposed resilience specification, not observed failure behavior. (`D`, `P`; [Search](https://help.superhuman.com/hc/en-us/articles/46005672652301-Search))

### Accessibility and performance targets

These are proposed acceptance targets, not measured Superhuman properties:

- **Keyboard completeness:** Every in-scope browsing operation has a discoverable keyboard route and a pointer route.
- **Semantic structure:** Expose split navigation, conversation focus/selection, expanded message state, dialogs, and attachment controls to assistive technology.
- **Visible focus:** Retain a non-color-only focus cue and explicit multi-selection state.
- **Announcements:** Announce result counts, selection counts, triage outcomes, and failures without reading the whole inbox repeatedly.
- **Contrast:** Use the sampled screenshot palette as a reference, not permission to reproduce inaccessible contrast.
- **Local response:** Aim for visible focus/selection feedback within 100 ms; measure rather than claiming parity with Superhuman.
- **Large lists:** Virtualize without invalidating keyboard navigation or screen-reader position; pagination must not silently change selection scope.

- **Attachments:** Preview dismissal, chooser behavior with multiple links/files, and OS-specific download flows.

Use fresh inputs for those observations, retain before/after evidence, and compare each declared behavior rather than only matching a screenshot. No such reconstruction verification has been performed in this investigation.

## 3. Tauri: conditional recommendation and the Electron tradeoff

**Conditional fit.** Tauri 2 supplies the desktop shell primitives (native system webviews, Rust↔frontend
IPC, capabilities, tray, notifications, shortcuts, deep links, signed updates) but **not** an email
architecture, a background daemon, a complete OAuth/token solution, or a safe mail renderer.

The core tradeoff: Tauri uses the OS webview (WKWebView on macOS, WebView2 on Windows, WebKitGTK on
Linux), avoiding a bundled Chromium but inheriting platform/version differences; Electron bundles
Chromium/Node for a consistent renderer baseline at the cost of footprint and heavier packaging. Neither
is automatically faster or safer; benchmark the actual workload.

Caveats: WebKit compatibility (focus, IME, typography, animation) needs early testing on real macOS
hardware — one isolated Intel Mac issue was reported in
[tauri#13141](https://github.com/tauri-apps/tauri/issues/13141), weak evidence of prevalence but
motivation for hardware testing. "Local-first" sync works while the process is alive, and a tray/menu-bar
mode can stay available after hiding the window, but **guaranteed sync while the app is fully quit is not
possible with Tauri async tasks alone** — that needs a separately designed helper or OS background
mechanism; decide quit-vs-hide semantics deliberately. Node-bound backend dependencies are not drop-in
(Rust backend), so a Node-heavy stack erodes Tauri's advantage. There is no official Tauri OAuth plugin;
treat community `tauri-plugin-oauth` as third-party and audit it before adoption. macOS distribution
requires code signing and, outside the App Store, notarization.

**Reconsider Electron or native if:** Chromium-consistent rendering across OS releases is a hard
requirement; product logic depends deeply on Node-only modules; guaranteed sync while quit is a core
promise; or the Rust/backend, hostile-email-security, and release-engineering work is not affordable.

---

## 4. Local-first architecture (proposed shape)

```
React/TS UI  →  narrow typed Tauri commands/events  →  Rust mail/sync core
                                                            │
                    SQLite (metadata + FTS5 search) ◄───────┤
                    OS secret store / Stronghold (tokens) ◄─┘
```

- **Trusted UI:** React/TypeScript; keyboard command system, list/detail, settings. Talks only through
  narrow typed commands and events.
- **Rust core:** OAuth callback handling, account/session state, provider integration (Gmail REST / IMAP /
  JMAP), MIME parsing, retryable sync coordinator, notifications, database and migrations.
- **Local store:** SQLite metadata + FTS5 search; prefer a Rust-owned DB API over exposing general SQL to
  the UI, and verify the chosen SQLite build actually enables FTS5 (Tauri's SQL plugin does not guarantee
  it). Async commands do not make a sync engine: cancellation, retries, incremental sync, conflict
  handling, backoff, and rate limits are application work.
- **Secrets:** tokens in the OS keychain (or Stronghold) — never in frontend storage or plain app config.

**Gmail full vs. incremental resync:** the sync design must handle both a full initial mailbox pull and
cheap incremental catch-up (history/sync APIs), including interruption/restart and duplicate-suppression.
Candidates document only partial answers (§2), so this must be designed explicitly.

**Durable queued actions and optimistic UI:** the desired UX is optimistic (read/archive/send reflected
instantly) with **durable local queues** so actions survive crashes, offline periods, and sync conflicts.
JakubSzwajka's `email` documents this pattern; it must be engineered deliberately (idempotent operations,
ordered retries, conflict resolution), not assumed.

**Untrusted mail rendering — the largest security obligation:** Tauri capabilities can confine a dedicated
message webview to zero privileged IPC, but they do **not** sanitize hostile HTML. Required: sanitized
HTML, scripts and forms stripped, remote images blocked or proxied by default, links opened externally
through an explicit handler, restrictive CSP, and never placing raw message markup into the privileged
app-origin DOM. Do not rely on an iframe as the security boundary (platform limits differ, notably
Linux/Android).

**OAuth flow:** authorization-code + PKCE in the system browser, random state, strict redirect/issuer
validation, one-shot loopback listener or deep-link return with a short timeout, refresh tokens never in
web storage.

**Personal vs. public OAuth verification:** personal use can qualify for a verification exception;
it does **not** inherently require leaving the OAuth consent screen in Testing status. External apps
in Testing generally receive seven-day refresh tokens for Gmail scopes; publishing status and scope
verification are separate considerations. Public distribution and server-side handling of restricted
Gmail data can introduce additional verification/security-assessment obligations. Validate the chosen
OAuth configuration rather than assuming weekly reauthentication is unavoidable. See Google's
[installed-app OAuth guidance](https://developers.google.com/identity/protocols/oauth2/native-app) and
[restricted-scope verification guidance](https://developers.google.com/identity/protocols/oauth2/production-readiness/restricted-scope-verification).

---

## 5. Android update (post-dates the research reports)

Newer findings, more current than the reports above:

- **Tauri 2 supports Android**, but **none of the inspected Tauri clients has a documented Android
  implementation**. The upstream `JakubSzwajka/email` repository has generated Android icons only;
  those assets do **not** establish Android support.
- **Inbox Zero does document Android product support** — see the
  [mobile apps docs](https://docs.getinboxzero.com/essentials/mobile-apps) and
  [the product page](https://www.getinboxzero.com/app);
  [getinboxzero.com/android](https://www.getinboxzero.com/android) redirects to
  [the Play Store listing](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.getinboxzero.app). Its
  public repository contains mobile **server APIs** but **no mobile app directory** under `apps/` — so
  forkable Android source / self-hosted mobile compatibility is **unverified**. Do not claim the client
  source is private or absent universally; it is simply not confirmed.
- Open option: whether Android needs **custom triage behavior** vs. mere **read/reply** capability is
  **unresolved**.

**Option A — custom desktop client + existing Android Gmail app.** Use the Gmail Android app with
provider-level labels/read/archive. Provider-level state syncs across devices, but any custom local state
— snooze queues, outbox queues, triage labels outside Gmail's model — needs **explicit cross-device
design** (e.g. Gmail labels as the sync medium, or accept desktop-only semantics). Lowest build cost;
keeps Android off the critical path.

**Option B — shared Tauri/Rust core with an Android-first spike.** Validate a shared core by prototyping
on Android first: auth (system browser/PKCE), read, send, background behavior, notifications. There is
**no automatic port** — desktop shell work and Android lifecycle/background/notification constraints are
separate engineering. Highest ceiling for a unified product; highest cost and risk.

The Tauri-vs-Electron and local-first decisions should be revisited after choosing between these options.

---

## 6. Small MVP and deferred scope

**Minimal MVP (suggested):** Gmail OAuth (PKCE, system browser) + secure token storage; sync one account
into SQLite with incremental catch-up; keyboard-first list/detail with optimized read, archive, reply;
durable outbox with optimistic send; isolated, sanitized message rendering.

**Deferred:** IMAP/Outlook providers, snooze/rules/Kanban workflows, unified multi-account inbox, Android
(pending the §5 decision), cross-device state, plugins/themes, signed/notarized distribution polish.

---

## 7. Build vs. fork: next steps

1. **Evaluate Pebble** if AGPL is acceptable and broader existing workflows are valuable
   (keyboard palette, snooze, rules, tray sync, Tantivy search). It is young; the static security review
   found renderer/privacy gaps that should be fixed and validated before primary-inbox use.
2. **Evaluate JakubSzwajka/email** for a narrower MIT-licensed Gmail/React foundation: early,
   macOS-only releases, bounded inbox window, no closed-app sync. Its static review found a
   recipient-expansion issue and send/retry integrity defects; address these before relying on it.
   Neither choice is cleared for primary-inbox use by these reviews.
3. If Windows/IMAP matters more, evaluate **Skim** first and add snooze/sync semantics deliberately.
4. Do not confuse wrapping with porting: embedding Zero/Inbox Zero in a Tauri webview preserves their
   backend dependencies; porting Mailspring means replacing Electron integration, not just repackaging.
5. Before importing real mail, validate: OAuth refresh/revocation, keychain behavior, hostile-HTML/CSP
   isolation, interrupted sync, duplicate-send prevention, MIME/attachments, offline mutations,
   large-inbox latency, and signing/update trust. Start with a disposable account.
6. Run the three recommended prototype spikes before any cross-platform commitment: (a) dense keyboard UI
   in WKWebView on real macOS hardware, (b) hostile-mail rendering spike in the isolated webview on a
   packaged build, (c) end-to-end local-first spike (OAuth → sync → FTS5 search → restart/network failure
   → hide/quit behavior).

**Unresolved questions:** Does Android need custom triage workflows, or is read/reply sufficient (§5)?
Option A vs. Option B for Android (§5)? Is AGPL (Pebble) acceptable for personal use? Is sync-while-quit
needed at all, or is tray/hide mode enough? Is platform-webview variance acceptable, or is a
Chromium-consistent Electron baseline required?

---

## 8. Security reviews (completed static pass)

Two independent subagent reviews are saved as separate, commit-pinned source-review reports:

- [`security/pebble-review.md`](security/pebble-review.md) — on QingJ01/Pebble at commit

- [`security/email-review.md`](security/email-review.md) — on JakubSzwajka/email at commit
  `f0af11852b27b17f229979a3e4e7e615a1f8c3dc`.

**Summary:** `email` has two P1 findings (contact-display-name recipient expansion and concurrent
outbox replay) plus five P2 integrity/cleanup findings. Pebble has four P2 findings concerning embedded
CSS visual containment, escaped CSS filtering, Strict-mode image URL handling, and a conditional
Unicode-header logging panic. The reports distinguish source-supported defects from untested runtime
consequences and additional hardening opportunities; their severity counts are not a comparative
security score.

The parent independently inspected the principal recipient, send/replay, and renderer/privacy source
paths. No project code, tests, builds, network exploit, or real mailbox was run. The findings are not
runtime demonstrations or comprehensive security certifications. Neither snapshot is recommended for
a primary inbox without fixes and targeted validation; Android requires its own review. Repository
snapshots were kept outside this workspace under `/tmp/email-security-review.PDYa6I/`; the reports
contain pinned GitHub links so their evidence does not depend on those temporary checkouts.

UX-05 needs more than selection UI. Durable per-conversation operations and exact Undo preimages already exist, but there’s no group record, and Undo only permits the newest individual operation. Calling the setters in a loop would leave only the last member undoable.

I’m scoping selection and durable groups together: Done/Not Done and explicit read/unread, per-member outcomes, and group Undo. Stars and all-mailbox selection stay out.

# UX-05 — Select and process several conversations safely

Status: **proposed implementation scope; not implemented or runtime-validated.**
Scoped against `ed6b2d2` after UX-04. Source requirements:
[UX spec](../superhuman-email-browsing-ux-spec.md) §List focus, opening, and
selection, §Context precedence, BROWSE-06/18; delivery boundary:
[implementation plan](superhuman-browsing-implementation-plan.md) §UX-05.
Build on [UX-03](ux-03-command-discovery.md) and
[UX-04](ux-04-trustworthy-undo.md), not a new mutation engine.

Everything below is a proposed engineering contract (`P`). The spec documents
multiselect shortcuts and bulk actions (`D`), but not these exact range,
transaction, recovery, or partial-Undo semantics. This is not a claim of
Superhuman equivalence or authorization to mutate a real mailbox.

## 1. Deliverable and boundaries

```text
Select three conversations → see “3 selected” and explicit action labels
→ Done → one durable group receipt → per-member pending/confirmed/failed/unknown
→ recover individual failures in Activity, or Z within 10 s for eligible members
→ restart → group and member outcomes remain inspectable
```

**Ship together:**

- Independent account-scoped selection, range anchor, count, pointer and keyboard
  controls in Inbox and cached Done.
- Bulk Done/Not Done and explicit Mark read/Mark unread through the shared
  action catalog, with the existing capability gates. Read remains Gmail-only;
  native fixture mode covers archive/unarchive groups, like the current setters.
- Bounded, idempotent, transactional **local group acceptance**, member receipts,
  immutable message targets and per-message preimages.
- Per-member status/recovery and one-level group Undo, including honest partial
  results. Reuse the serial worker, provider setters and reconciliation.

**Do not include:** stars (the star portion of BROWSE-06 is deferred), labels,
move, trash, reminders, new provider permissions, multiple accounts/providers,
new browsing contexts, all-matching/cross-page selection, concurrent provider
execution, a Gmail batch endpoint, arbitrary action execution, HTML rendering,
auto-read, redo or multi-level Undo. No composer/send changes. No state-framework
or worker replacement. Selection itself need not survive restart; accepted
intent and its recovery records must.

## 2. Source facts and required changes

| Current source | UX-05 consequence |
|---|---|
| `useMailbox.ts` has `focusedRef`, `openRef`, stable-ID focus resolution and context/session fences, but no selection. | Add selected references and range anchor independently; reuse account/context fencing and focus fallback. |
| `InboxList.vue` uses list/listitem, roving focus and `aria-current`; plain click opens, row actions stop propagation. | Add explicit selection controls without conflating DOM focus with selected state or breaking compact-row overflow handling. |
| `App.vue::actionTarget` resolves one explicit/focused/reader target. | Replace shared conversation-action resolution with an immutable target list; explicit inline row actions still resolve exactly one row. |
| `submitMutation` and `inFlightCommandRef` track a single target; `LastAction`/`ActionNotice` describe one operation. | Introduce an explicit single-or-group pending/notice model; do not use the first selected ref as a fake group identity. |
| Gmail `accept_new_operation` opens a transaction around `accept_operation_tx`; fixture `Store::set_archived` owns its transaction. | Extract transaction-local acceptance helpers, retaining existing checks, for one bounded group transaction. Calling public setters in a loop is insufficient. |
| Gmail acceptance already persists immutable targets, effective per-message preimages and recovery snapshots; targets are bounded to 1000 messages per operation. | Preserve those limits/semantics for each member; never re-resolve inventory during execution, retry or Undo. |
| Both stores' Undo eligibility uses the newest non-compensating **operation**. | A loop would supersede every member except the last. Model a group as one top-level user action before exposing group Undo. |
| Activity contains individual operations, including recovery after rows leave Inbox; there is no durable group/query contract. | Persist group membership and expose group detail independently of current list rows and operation-history truncation. |

These are static source observations, not a new certification of existing code.

## 3. Selection and dispatch contract

### 3.1 State and exact interactions

Use account + conversation identity (`ConversationRef`), never indexes or a bare
conversation ID. Suggested state: `selectedRefs` (keyed set/map) and
`rangeAnchorRef`. Indexes are temporary inputs for movement/range calculation.

| Input | Result |
|---|---|
| `X` on a list-owned focused row | Toggle that row, keep focus there, set range anchor there. Ignore auto-repeat. |
| Plain `J/K` (existing arrow aliases unchanged) | Move focus only, no wrap, no selection changes. |
| `Shift+J/K` | Move one row and add the inclusive anchor-to-destination range; if no valid anchor, start at the pre-move focused row. Boundary is a no-op. |
| Cmd-click row | Toggle that row and move focus/anchor there; do not open it. |
| Shift-click row | Add the inclusive anchor-to-clicked range and focus the clicked row; retain the anchor. If missing, use the pre-click focus, otherwise the clicked row alone. |
| Cmd+Shift-click | Same range behavior as Shift-click. |
| Row selection checkbox | Toggle only that row, set anchor there, never open it. |
| Plain row click / Enter | Existing open behavior; do not silently clear or widen selection. Enter on a native control retains native behavior. |
| Clear selection | Clear set and anchor, do not navigate. |

Range extension is **additive**: reversing direction does not subtract already
selected rows. This is a deliberate completion choice, not observed target
behavior. Date headings never participate. Hover never selects or marks read.

Provide **Select all loaded (N)** and **Clear selection** as discoverable pointer
controls and palette commands. Select-all snapshots only currently loaded rows,
not the exact-total count or unseen pages. Later page loads/new arrivals do not
join automatically. Proposed bound: **100 selected conversations per action**;
if more rows are loaded, disable Select all loaded with a visible explanation
and reject additions beyond 100 without replacing the existing selection. Never
silently take the first 100. This is a product/safety bound, not a provider limit.

### 3.2 Navigation and refresh

- Escape order: existing top overlay/disclosure/drawer → selected set → reader
  or context Back. Clearing selection does not also leave the current surface.
- Keep selection on reader open/return within the same browsing context, never
  extending it from reader J/K. Show its count and bulk scope in the reader too;
  hidden selection must never cause a surprising bulk action.
- Context/account changes clear selection and anchor; Back to a prior context
  restores navigation, **not** its old selected set. Disconnect/session changes
  fence outstanding receipts so old-account notices cannot repopulate the UI.
- A successful authoritative list refresh intersects selection with surviving
  loaded refs and clears an absent anchor. Loading/errors must not be mistaken
  for an authoritative empty result. Preserve existing stable-ID focus and scroll
  behavior; background refresh must not steal focus.
- At dispatch, freeze the exact selected references in current loaded order.
  The action's persisted member list, not the live selection, drives subsequent
  progress/recovery. Rows removed by a pending overlay may leave selection;
  they must not disappear from the group result surface.
- Definitively failed/rejected members stay reachable in Activity, even if no
  longer present in the active list. Provide per-item Open/Retry as applicable;
  never silently reselect them or include them in the user's next selection.

### 3.3 One target policy

Shared toolbar, palette and conversation-action shortcuts resolve:

1. Explicit inline row action → exactly that row, regardless of selected set.
2. Otherwise nonempty selection → exactly that set, even in the reader.
3. Otherwise existing focused/open conversation behavior.

Use the group path whenever selection is nonempty, even for one selected row.
Label selected-scope actions with the count; reader conversation triage controls
must use the same visible scope. Opening, copying contacts, message navigation,
and Reply are not bulk operations; Reply retains its existing source checks.
Bulk archive must not invoke single-reader “archive and advance” behavior.

Offer explicit **Mark N read** / **Mark N unread**, never a mixed-state toggle.
Existing inline single-row read toggling remains row-scoped. Selection actions
only intercept keys when the list owns them, and preserve IME, inputs,
contenteditable, buttons/links and top-surface precedence. No unconditional
global Cmd+A interception. Block duplicate mutation dispatch while acceptance
or its receipt recovery is unresolved; navigation can remain usable.

## 4. Durable group contract

### 4.1 Local acceptance is atomic; remote execution is not

A group contains one setter kind/value (archive, unarchive, read or unread)
and 1–100 unique refs from the active account. Validate structure, duplicates,
bounds, request ID, active account and capability before accepting anything.
Malformed/cross-account/unauthorized commands reject the whole request.

In **one SQLite transaction**:

1. Check a canonical fingerprint (kind, value, canonical member identities) and
   account-scoped group request ID. Same request/payload returns the original
   receipt; changed payload returns `request_id_conflict`. Preserve the original
   persisted member ordering on replay. Define collision handling with existing
   setter/Undo request IDs; no accidental cross-command receipt reuse.
2. Persist the group header, acceptance time and ordered member manifest.
3. For each member, accept an ordinary child operation with immutable message
   targets, effective preimages and recovery snapshot, using the existing checks.
   A member that is gone/unactionable or exceeds the existing target bound gets
   a persisted **rejected** acceptance result and typed reason, not a fabricated
   failed provider operation. Use prevalidation or member savepoints so rejected
   members leave no partial targets/preimages/request rows behind.
4. Persist the original receipt, including accepted operation IDs and rejected
   members; commit once. Wake the worker only after commit.

Storage/transaction failure rolls back **the entire local acceptance**. Even an
all-rejected valid request has an idempotent durable receipt, with zero child
operations. It does not supersede a previously undoable action. Accepted child
operations run serially as today; group acceptance does not promise atomic
provider application or rollback of successful siblings on failure.

Recheck mutation capability at execution as today. Disconnection, cache eviction
and restart must not orphan durable group/target/recovery records. Preserve the
existing Gmail interrupted-dispatch uncertainty behavior; do not blindly replay
an applying mutation as confirmed success.

### 4.2 Data and typed boundary

Add durable group header/request/member tables in **both stores**, with account
isolation, stable member ordinal, group-to-operation linkage and persisted
acceptance rejections. Record group Undo requests and per-member decisions too.
Migration must preserve existing operations, requests, preimages and Undo links.

Proposed named seams (freeze exact Rust DTOs/error shapes and regenerate TS
before UI integration; these names are not existing APIs):

- `set_archived_group`: account, refs, explicit `archived`, request ID.
- `set_read_group`: account, refs, explicit `read`, request ID; Gmail-only.
- `get_operation_group`: active-account lookup by original request ID, returning
  optional committed group, immutable acceptance receipt and current member
  statuses/Undo availability. This also resolves a lost acceptance response.
- `list_operation_groups`: bounded recent group summaries with cursor, independent
  of Inbox/Done rows; supplies Activity and restart recovery. Known group detail
  remains directly addressable even when absent from the recent page.
- `undo_operation_group`: group ID and request ID; durable per-member outcome.

A member result distinguishes `rejected` at acceptance from an accepted operation's
`queued`, `applying`, `confirmed`, `failed`, `outcome_unknown` or `cancelled` status.
Group counts are derived from members; accepted is not succeeded. Keep compensation
statuses separate from original execution statuses. Include group linkage on
operation summaries so existing Activity retry/open paths remain usable and group
members cannot misleadingly advertise individual Undo.

Use narrow MailClient methods, Rust-generated types, transport validation/tests,
and explicit Tauri commands, command manifest, capabilities and permissions.
Never expose arbitrary group actions/SQL/provider mutations. Browser fake models
these outcomes but continues to disclose that it is in-memory and non-durable.

### 4.3 Lost responses and recovery

The UI retains the original request ID and immutable command until acceptance is
resolved. A rejected IPC promise alone does not establish that nothing committed.
Query by request ID and/or replay **that exact request**, never invent a fresh
request to recover an ambiguous acceptance. Show “Acceptance not yet known” until
resolved; distinguish this transport state from a member's provider outcome unknown.
On restart, recent groups are discoverable through Activity without a frontend
receipt. A not-yet-committed lookup is not permission to submit a different request.

Individual retries reuse the existing immutable-target retry path. They are new
top-level user actions, linked to the original member for inspection; they do not
rewrite the historical group receipt. Unknown members retain the existing warning
to verify state before retry. No automatic Retry all or blind replay of successes.

## 5. Group Undo and single-action compatibility

Keep one-level **latest user action on the account** and the 10-second Rust-clock
window; do not relax to arbitrary same-target history. A group is one action,
not N mutually superseding operations. Introduce a shared action-order identity
(or equivalent transactionally ordered representation) for singles, groups and
retries; timestamp comparison alone is insufficient. Existing historical singles
retain their order/eligibility semantics.

- All accepted children share the group's acceptance time/deadline and top-level
  action identity. Children and compensations cannot be individually undone via
  `undo_operation`; prevent a last-child escape around group eligibility.
- A newer single action/group/individual retry supersedes the older group, and
  a newer group supersedes the older single. Compensation is not a new user
  action. Undoing the latest action does not reopen earlier history.
- Within the latest group's window, evaluate each accepted member under the
  existing status/preimage checks. Queued → atomic cancel; applying/confirmed →
  ordered compensation, at most two operations per member for mixed prior values.
  Targets/preimages come from original acceptance, never current inventory.
- Persist skipped members and reasons: acceptance rejected, failed (overlay
  already dropped), unknown outcome, unknown prior values, or already undone.
  Eligible siblings can still be undone. Expiry/supersession rejects the whole
  group Undo without changes. An all-ineligible group offers no enabled Undo.
- Validate and persist all member decisions, cancellations and compensations in
  **one transaction**, with worker-claim races handled under the same store lock.
  Group Undo has its own idempotent request/receipt. A retry with the same request
  returns the same decisions, not a new pass over changing member statuses.
- One Undo attempt per group; skipped members are not silently retried if later
  reconciled. Activity remains their recovery route. No redo.
- Say “Undo accepted for 2 of 3; 1 skipped — outcome unknown”, not “Restored 3”.
  Cancelling queued intent is immediately local; compensating intent is pending
  until confirmed. Failed/unknown compensation must remain visible per member.

## 6. UI, accessibility and recovery surfaces

- Distinct row selection marker **and** lavender focus cue; selection cannot be
  color-only. Prefer native labelled checkboxes within the existing list/listitem
  structure; expose checked state without adding invalid `aria-selected` to list
  items. Keep `aria-current` for focus. Checkboxes and row controls stop propagation.
- Add a compact selection action bar with count, explicit desired-state actions,
  Select all loaded/Clear, and honest bound/loaded-scope wording. Preserve compact
  rows at larger text sizes and the existing narrow-desktop action disclosures.
- Extend the single-slot notice to single-or-group identity. It shows accepted,
  pending, confirmed, failed, rejected, unknown and cancelled counts separately
  with an Activity/detail route; aggregate wording never hides partial failure.
  After a newer action replaces the slot, older groups remain in Activity.
- Extend Activity with group headers/detail and per-member Open/Retry plus Undo
  results. Preserve existing standalone-operation history and compensation links;
  no failure may be lost because its conversation left the current context.
- Rust supplies Undo deadlines/eligibility; UI timers are advisory. On restart,
  rehydrate the latest eligible single/group notice from authoritative state.
  Older group members must not be re-pointed as standalone undoable actions.
- Announce selection count and concise outcomes through a polite live region,
  not the entire list. Preserve normal tab order, button keyboard activation,
  focus on Clear/empty-list transitions, and Back/Activity reachability.

## 7. Acceptance and validation

### Rust/store/provider tests (both stores where supported)

1. Noncontiguous refs are accepted once; insert/reorder conversations and add a
   reply after acceptance → execution/Undo still touch only original message IDs.
2. Structural invalidity, cross-account targets, duplicates, bounds and denied
   capabilities → no group/child writes. Member unavailable → persisted rejection,
   valid siblings accepted. All-rejected case preserves prior Undo eligibility.
3. Inject transaction failure mid-group → no partial group/children/preimages;
   same request retry is safe. Member-savepoint rollback leaves no orphan data.
4. Same request replay before/after restart gives identical receipt; changed payload
   conflicts. Lost response + lookup/replay creates no duplicate children.
5. Three members: confirmed, definitively failed, outcome unknown → separate
   statuses, correct overlays, no rollback of successful siblings. Restart/reconcile
   retains group linkage, recovery snapshots and original immutable targets.
6. Group Undo at 9 seconds: queued cancel, applying/confirmed compensation; mixed
   read preimages restore independently, non-INBOX sent messages stay out, new
   replies remain untouched. Unknown/failed/rejected/prior-unknown siblings are
   explicitly skipped. Worker-claim race cannot produce duplicate compensation.
7. Expiry at 10 seconds, newer single/group/retry supersession, child single-Undo
   bypass, duplicate Undo request, second different Undo request, compensation
   failure/unknown, restart inside/outside window. Older history never reopens.
8. Migration preserves UX-04 single-action behavior and historical requests;
   cached Done evidence remains correct for cancelled/compensated group members.
9. Group detail/list pagination/account fencing; a group absent from a recent page
   is still queryable by request identity. Revoked capabilities fail closed.

### Frontend/transport/rendered tests

- X toggle/no-repeat, J/K focus-only, range extension/reversal/bounds, Cmd/Shift
  click, checkbox propagation, nonselectable headings, maximum-selection messaging.
- New arrival, reorder, page load, transient errors, context Back and account
  changes never widen or leak selection. Reader round trip retains only explicit
  IDs; Escape clears before leaving. Typing shortcuts/IME cannot mutate mail.
- Exact shared targets versus row-scoped actions; mixed read actions are explicit;
  selected-one uses group semantics. Reader banner matches scope; bulk archive
  never accidentally calls the single-reader advance path.
- Per-member failure/unknown display, retained original request on lost response,
  partial Undo wording and compensation progress, restart rehydration, Activity
  recovery independent of visible rows. Browser fake parity without durability claims.
- Native command/envelope and error validation tests; generated-contract check.
- Rendered layout/focus regression at the existing desktop/contact breakpoints
  and enlarged text; checkbox/toolbar operation does not break row disclosures or
  reader/list scroll restoration.

**Spec checkpoint:** BROWSE-06 for archive, BROWSE-18 for partial execution;
regress BROWSE-07/08/10/17/20. Stars remain explicitly unfulfilled.

Run the six checks in `.pi/factory.json` and native compile/bridge checks where

Scoped in **[docs/ux-05-safe-bulk-processing.md](docs/ux-05-safe-bulk-processing.md)** and linked from the roadmap. No application code changed.

### Included
- Independent selection using X, Shift+J/K, Cmd/Shift-click and checkboxes.
- Visible selected count, **Select all loaded**, and Clear selection.
- Bulk Done/Not Done and explicit Mark read/Mark unread.
- Durable, idempotent group acceptance with immutable per-conversation targets.
- Per-member pending, confirmed, failed and unknown outcomes, recoverable through Activity.
- Group Undo within 10 seconds, with explicit partial results and skip reasons.

### Key implementation issue
Current Undo permits only the newest **individual operation**. Calling existing setters in a loop would leave only the last conversation undoable. UX-05 must treat the group as one user action while reusing existing execution and reconciliation.

### Recommended scope decisions
1. Cap selection/groups at **100 loaded conversations**; no all-mailbox selection.
2. Make local acceptance transactional; do **not** promise atomic remote execution.
3. Keep latest-action-only Undo, allowing eligible group members to restore while reporting skipped members.
4. Preserve selection through reader visits with visible bulk scope; clear it on context/account changes.

**Excluded:** stars, labels, trash, reminders, new provider permissions and multi-level Undo.

name: pi-subagents
description: |
  Delegate work to Pi subagents after the operator asks for it: one child,
  parallel or scripted workflows, async runs, resume/steer/stop, review fanout,
